beats.say: On November twelfth, a Microsoft outage cut people off from Microsoft three sixty five for about thirty hours.
Microsoft hasn't said exactly what broke. But here's why one failure hits so many people.
Cloud email isn't one computer. It's giant shared server farms, holding huge numbers of mailboxes.
They lean on shared parts, like login and routing servers. If one of those stumbles, everything behind it stalls.
Then every app retries at once, and that pile of retries can slow the recovery.
So what about email sent during the outage? Email has a safety net. Email's rule book, called SMTP, says a server that can't deliver
a message must queue it and try again. It should wait at least thirty minutes between tries, and keep going for at least four to five days.
When service came back, the waiting mail poured in. Microsoft says that backlog has now been processed.
